irr.title: Irrigation planner
irr.subtitle: Tells you how much water each field needs and when, from today's weather.
irr.volume: ≈ {m3} m³ of water — about {hours} hours with a 2-inch pump (8 litres per second)
irr.rainExpected: No irrigation needed — rain expected {day} ({mm} mm)
irr.beyondIrrigate: If no rain falls, next irrigation around {day} (about {mm} mm)
irr.drainNow: Drain the field now — harvest is less than 2 weeks away
irr.stop: Crop is ready for harvest — no irrigation needed
irr.rainfedNote: This field is marked rainfed — give this water only if you have a pump or canal.
irr.et0Help: How much water the air takes from a grass field today, in mm. Hot, sunny, windy, dry days are higher.
irr.etcHelp: Water your crop uses today (ET₀ × crop factor). 1 mm = 10,000 litres per hectare.
irr.kcHelp: Crop factor (Kc) from FAO tables — it changes with growth stage. Your crop is {days} days old.
irr.rain7Help: Forecast rain for the coming week, weighted by the chance of rain.
irr.tawHelp: Water the root zone can store ({depth} m deep). Irrigate when about {raw} mm has been used.
irr.planUplandHint: Bars: water used and rain. Line: how dry the soil is (higher = drier). Red line: irrigate.
irr.planPaddyHint: Bars: water used and rain. Line: water level in the field (cm). Red line: 15 cm below the soil.
irr.awdHelp: Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD): let the water sink to 15 cm below the soil before re-flooding. It saves 15–30% of water and pumping cost with no yield loss (IRRI).

awd.establishment: Keep 3–5 cm of water for the first 2 weeks after transplanting.
awd.awd: Safe AWD: let the water drop to 15 cm below the soil, then flood again to 5 cm.
awd.flowering: Flowering time: keep 3–5 cm of standing water — do not let the field dry.
awd.drain: Drain the field 10–14 days before harvest so it is dry for harvesting.
awd.none: No paddy water advice for this stage.

irr.awdTube: Check with a field water tube: a 30 cm plastic pipe with holes, pushed 15 cm into the soil.
irr.waterAbove: Water is {cm} cm above the soil
irr.waterBelow: Water is {cm} cm below the soil
irr.methodUpland: We add up the water your crop uses each day (FAO-56 method: ET₀ × crop factor) and take away useful rain and your logged irrigation. When the soil has lost the safe amount of water for your crop and soil type, we tell you to irrigate enough to fill it back up.
irr.methodPaddy: We track the water level in your paddy each day: rain and irrigation raise it; crop use and seepage lower it. Following IRRI's safe AWD rule, we tell you to irrigate when the water falls 15 cm below the soil (or below 3 cm at planting and flowering).
irr.noFields: Add a field to get an irrigation plan.

ins.explain: Weather-index insurance pays out automatically when measured rainfall at your farm crosses the agreed limit — no field inspection needed.

ins.basisRiskHelp: Index insurance pays on measured weather, not on your actual loss. Sometimes your field is damaged but the index does not trigger (or the other way round). This is called basis risk.
ins.requested: Request sent — the insurer will contact you.
ins.indicative: Amounts are indicative, based on the insurer's current policies for your crop. Final terms come from the insurer.
ins.nextSteps: An agent will call you to confirm your fields and explain the payout rules.
